claims.text: The induction-melted as-cast alloy has a metastable solid-solution matrix coexisting with early-formed intermetallic precipitates.
Slow cooling combined with an isothermal hold will selectively transform the metastable solid-solution matrix into stable intermetallic phases.
The phases produced by the thermal treatment will specifically include Mg-rich intermetallics.
The phases produced by the thermal treatment will specifically include Al/Ti-enriched intermetallics.
The controlled thermal intervention accelerates transformation toward a more thermodynamically stable phase assemblage.
The evolving Mg-rich and Al/Ti-enriched intermetallic phases act as nucleation sites for stable, adherent surface-passivation layers.
Thermally induced phase reorganization enriches the alloy surface in elements that promote protective oxide-film formation.
The resulting protective films mitigate corrosive attack.
The resulting surface films modify oxidation kinetics at elevated temperature.
The thermally treated alloy will have a higher volume fraction of stable intermetallic phases than the as-cast baseline.
The thermally treated alloy will exhibit lower corrosion current density than the rapidly quenched as-cast baseline.
The thermally treated alloy will exhibit a distinct high-temperature oxidation mass-change profile relative to the as-cast baseline.
A distinct oxidation mass-change profile will indicate improved or altered passivation behavior.
The rapidly quenched as-cast baseline has inferior or less-controlled corrosion and oxidation behavior.
The proposed mechanism applies to induction-melted Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys with density below 6 g/cm3 and solid-solution/intermetallic coexistence.
Significant deviations in composition or processing may cause the proposed mechanism not to hold.
Failure to produce an appreciable intermetallic-phase increase together with no reproducible corrosion or oxidation difference from the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts transformation into 'specific' Mg-rich and Al/Ti-enriched intermetallic phases, while the uncertainty field states that the identity of the relevant intermetallic phases remains undetermined.
